root_cause.text: In fs/iomap/buffered-io.c, iomap_read_folio_iter() incorrectly kept ctx->cur_folio valid for !ifs folios unless bytes_submitted equaled the full folio size, so when I/O was issued at a smaller granularity than i_blkbits/folio size, iomap_read_end() later accessed a folio already handed off to the I/O helper.
root_cause.evidence: The commit message states that when “1 << inode->i_blkbits matches the folio size but is different from the granularity used for the IO,” less-than-full-folio I/O can occur for the !ifs case, causing `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len) ctx->cur_folio = NULL;` not to run; the patch fixes this by changing the condition to `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len || !ifs) ctx->cur_folio = NULL;` and explicitly says otherwise “iomap_read_end() will still be called on the folio even though the IO helper owns it.”

intent_record.intent_summary: Declare a local `iomap_folio_state` pointer in `iomap_read_folio_iter()` to support forthcoming folio state handling logic.
intent_record.what: A new local variable declaration, `struct iomap_folio_state *ifs;`, was added inside `iomap_read_folio_iter()` alongside the existing local variables.
intent_record.how: At runtime this change alone does not alter behavior, but it prepares the function to use an `iomap_folio_state` pointer later in the function, likely to support additional folio state handling logic.

intent_record.intent_summary: Assign the result of ifs_alloc to ifs so the read-folio path uses the newly allocated state instead of dropping it.
intent_record.what: The call to ifs_alloc(iter->inode, folio, iter->flags) was changed from a standalone expression to an assignment storing its return value in the variable ifs.
intent_record.how: This change preserves the object or pointer returned by ifs_alloc for subsequent use in the function, enabling later code to operate on the allocated state instead of discarding the result and potentially using an uninitialized or stale ifs value.

intent_record.intent_summary: Fix folio ownership handoff in `iomap_read_folio_iter()` so the IO helper takes over when no `ifs` is attached, even if the whole folio was not submitted at once.
intent_record.what: The condition that clears `ctx->cur_folio` in `iomap_read_folio_iter()` was changed from `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len)` to `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len || !ifs)`, and the surrounding comment was updated to document two ownership handoff cases, including when no `ifs` is attached to the folio.
intent_record.how: At runtime, folio ownership is now handed off to the IO helper not only when the full folio has been submitted for IO, but also when there is no `ifs` associated with the folio. This prevents the current context from retaining ownership in a case where IO is performed at a smaller granularity than the folio size, avoiding incorrect folio completion handling.

consistency_review.core_intent: Fix folio state/ownership handling in the iomap read-folio path so newly allocated state is retained and IO ownership is correctly handed off when no ifs is attached.

relevance_review.reason: This change only introduces a local `iomap_folio_state` pointer declaration as preparation for later logic; it does not alter the handling of `ctx->cur_folio`, folio lifetime, or the bytes_submitted/full-folio condition that caused the bug.

The changes directly match the root cause: they fix how `iomap_read_folio_iter()` manages folio state and ownership when no `ifs` is attached, including handing ownership to the I/O helper even for partial-folio submission, which is exactly the buggy condition described.

candidates.rationale: This condition is the core bug: it only relinquishes ctx->cur_folio when the submitted I/O covers the full folio, so for !ifs folios submitted in smaller chunks, ctx->cur_folio incorrectly remains valid and can later be accessed after ownership was handed to the I/O helper.

This statement performs the folio ownership handoff, but only under the overly strict full-folio submission condition. As a result, it is skipped for partial submissions, leaving a stale ctx->cur_folio that iomap_read_end() may later access.

vuln_statements.explanation: This conditional is the root cause because it only clears ctx->cur_folio when the submitted I/O length equals the full folio length. For !ifs folios submitted in smaller chunks, ownership had already been handed to the I/O helper, but this condition prevented clearing ctx->cur_folio, leaving a stale folio pointer later accessed by iomap_read_end().

bic_trace_step.reason: The diff is sufficient because it shows the exact logic in the vulnerable path: `iomap_read_folio_iter()`, the `ctx->cur_folio` lifetime handling, and the final call site in `iomap_read_folio()`. The fix described by the root cause is present. In `iomap_read_folio_iter()`, after `*bytes_submitted += plen;`, the code now explicitly invalidates the current folio when all bytes of the folio have been handed to the IO helper: `if (*bytes_submitted == folio_len) ctx->cur_folio = NULL;`. This directly addresses the bug where `ctx->cur_folio` was previously kept valid for `!ifs` folios after handoff. The final caller also now guards the end-of-read handling with `if (ctx->cur_folio) iomap_read_end(ctx->cur_folio, bytes_submitted);`, which avoids later accessing a folio that may already have been ended by the IO helper. Additionally, `iomap_read_end()`'s `!ifs` branch now asserts that it should only be called with no submitted bytes: `WARN_ON_ONCE(bytes_submitted); folio_unlock(folio);`, matching the fixed ownership rule. Therefore the vulnerable construct is absent in this commit version, and the fix is present.
